chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir and al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, who said:

Al-Nabaji entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'What do you say about a person in ihram who touched his beard and two hairs fell from it?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Even if I touched my beard and ten hairs fell from it, there would be no penalty upon me.'

These two reports are interpreted as applying to one who did not deliberately pluck any of the hair, because whenever he did that deliberately, the expiation would be incumbent upon him, according to what we have previously stated. That will be clarified - what he narrated:

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ihram (consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for an ihram pilgrer who accidentally touches and loses beard hair?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between accidental hair loss due to simple touching and deliberate plucking (*nathf*) while in *ihram*, ruling that no expiation (*kaffarah*) is due for the former. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor, unintentional acts do not incur penalty, reserving the obligation for intentional transgression of *ihram* conditions. The text further notes that these reports are understood to apply specifically to cases lacking deliberate intent, aligning with broader legal maxims regarding negligence versus action.
